title: The full product is the limit of a finite-prefix tower
statement: Let $A:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be a tower and $s\in\mathbf N$. For $T_s(A)_n=\prod_{i<n+s}A_i$ with restriction transitions [lem-pc-roos-finite-prefix-construction], the cone with vertex $\prod_{i\in\mathbf N}A_i$ and prefix restriction maps is a limit cone. For any cone $c$, the value of coordinate $i$ extracted from level $n$ is independent of $n$ whenever $i<n+s$.

proof.text: For any two prefixes containing i, compare both with the prefix indexed by their maximum. The cone naturality equations imply equality of the two extracted coordinate maps.

Define the map from a cone vertex to the infinite product by extracting coordinate i from level i+1, which contains i for all s. Prefix compatibility proves the cone factorization equations coordinatewise. Any map satisfying them has those same coordinates, so product extensionality proves uniqueness.
